name: Crooked Fingers
label: Merge
lede: Eric Bachmann walked out of Archers of Loaf's noise with a CB-radio handle for a band name, then wrote dark, gorgeous songs from a Seattle cargo van, a Denver sandwich cart and a Taipei classroom.

eras.title: Out of the Archers' wreckage
eras.text: Archers of Loaf had worn Eric Bachmann out by 1998. He slowed everything down, dropped the shouting for a low croon, and made Crooked Fingers a vehicle for his songs with whoever was around, first on Athens' WARM label and then at Merge Records.

years.src: Wikipedia: Eric Bachmann · Wikipedia: Crooked Fingers
years.h: Archers of Loaf break up; Eric Bachmann starts Crooked Fingers
years.p: Touring exhaustion ends [[Archers of Loaf|7cf05db3-24e7-4534-84bf-65006cd0cc82]] in late 1998. Eric Bachmann starts Crooked Fingers as a solo venture, taking the name from his grandfather's CB radio handle.
years.xp: Bachmann was born in Greensboro, North Carolina, in 1970 and started out as a saxophone major at Appalachian State. Between Archers records he'd already made instrumental albums as Barry Black, with help from [[Ben Folds|51b7f46f-6c0f-46f2-9496-08c9ec2624d4]] among others.

years.h: Crooked Fingers, the debut on WARM Records
years.p: Crooked Fingers' first album comes out on Athens, Georgia's WARM Records. The noise of [[Archers of Loaf|7cf05db3-24e7-4534-84bf-65006cd0cc82]] is gone; Eric Bachmann's songs are slow and acoustic, sung low.

years.h: Bring On the Snakes, the second WARM album
years.p: Crooked Fingers' second album, Bring On the Snakes, is the last before Eric Bachmann signs with Merge Records.

years.h: Reservoir Songs: Neil Diamond and Queen, Merge debut
years.p: Crooked Fingers' first Merge release is a covers EP, with Eric Bachmann taking on songs by Neil Diamond and Queen.

years.h: Red Devil Dawn, the first full-length on Merge
years.p: Crooked Fingers' first full-length for Merge Records follows the Reservoir Songs covers EP, and Merge stays Eric Bachmann's home for most of the band's run.

eras.title: A van in Ballard, a cart in Denver
eras.text: The best-reviewed Crooked Fingers record arrived just as the money ran out. Eric Bachmann responded by moving into a cargo van, then into a relationship in Colorado, then onto a sandwich cart, and finally into self-releasing his next album.

years.h: Dignity and Shame, with a song named for a killer bull
years.p: Co-produced with Seattle's Martin Feveyear, Dignity and Shame opens with Islero, named for the bull that killed Spanish matador Manolete. Its song Sleep All Summer outlived the record.
years.xp: Sleep All Summer took on a life of its own: [[The National|664c3e0e-42d8-48c1-b209-1efca19c0325]] covered it with [[St. Vincent|5334edc0-5faf-4ca5-b1df-000de3e1f752]] for a Merge compilation, and [[Neko Case|e13d2935-8c42-4c0a-96d7-654062acf106]] recorded it for Hell-On in 2018 with Eric Bachmann singing along.

years.cap: On the Dignity and Shame tour the band carried its instruments into the room
years.h: Crooked Fingers carry their instruments into the crowd
years.p: On the Dignity and Shame tour, every musician pulls their instrument off the stage and plays a few songs from the middle of the audience. Old Archers bassist Matt Gentling is on bass.

years.cap: A futon, a cassette recorder and a YMCA membership
years.h: Eric Bachmann lives in a Ford cargo van in Seattle
years.p: Broke after a money-losing full-band tour, Eric Bachmann gives up his Seattle apartment and lives about eight months in a white 1999 Ford E150 with a futon in the back.
years.xp:
He parked on quiet streets in Crown Hill and Ballard, wrote all day in Golden Gardens and Discovery Park, showered at the YMCA and used a 24-hour Kinko's on Market Street for late-night bathroom runs. He told Willamette Week he drank hard at first, got depressed, quit, and put himself on a strict routine.

The songs came fast: a record's worth in about two months. On a solo tour, someone broke into the van in a Columbia, Missouri, hotel lot; Bachmann swung a tire iron, and the intruder grabbed it and ran.

years.h: The van songs become Eric Bachmann's solo album To the Races
years.p: The songs Eric Bachmann wrote living in his van come out under his own name as To the Races, not as Crooked Fingers.

q: A great woman... she's the reason I moved there.
years.h: Eric Bachmann sells Cuban sandwiches from a cart in Denver
years.p: Eric Bachmann moves to Colorado for a woman and spends a summer running a Cuban sandwich cart for steady money, until touring offers from [[Neko Case|e13d2935-8c42-4c0a-96d7-654062acf106]] pull him back on the road.

Turning down label deals, Crooked Fingers put out Forfeit/Fortune themselves through Constant Artists and Red Pig. [[Neko Case|e13d2935-8c42-4c0a-96d7-654062acf106]] sings on it, alongside [[Silver Jews|1bc2d696-c0e2-480d-87ed-17b2a82d7983]] drummer Brian Kotzur.
years.xp: Mark Nevers and Alex McManus co-produced. Reviews were lukewarm: Pitchfork gave it 5.2.

eras.title: Written in Taipei
eras.text: The last Crooked Fingers album for fifteen years was written half a world away and landed the same year Archers of Loaf came back from the dead.

years.h: Archers of Loaf reunite at an unannounced show
years.p: Twelve years after the split, [[Archers of Loaf|7cf05db3-24e7-4534-84bf-65006cd0cc82]] play a surprise show in January 2011, and Eric Bachmann is back fronting his old band.

years.src: Wikipedia: Breaks in the Armor · Wikipedia: Eric Bachmann
years.h: Breaks in the Armor, written while teaching in Taipei
years.p: Eric Bachmann wrote it while teaching English in Taipei, Taiwan, then recorded in Athens, Georgia, with Liz Durrett, now his wife, singing. It reaches No. 23 on Billboard's Heatseekers chart.
years.xp: Liz Durrett is the niece of [[Vic Chesnutt|b07cdbbe-421e-418a-bbb7-ce0d8d53bfa8]]. The A.V. Club called these some of the most melodious songs Bachmann had recorded.

eras.title: A sideman, a solo name, a louder old band
eras.text: Crooked Fingers went quiet. Eric Bachmann played guitar behind Neko Case, made a record under his own name, retired the band's name and brought Archers of Loaf all the way back to the studio.

years.h: Eric Bachmann joins Neko Case's touring band
years.p: Eric Bachmann spends 2013 to 2016 in [[Neko Case|e13d2935-8c42-4c0a-96d7-654062acf106]]'s touring band.

years.h: Eric Bachmann retires the Crooked Fingers name
years.p: Eric Bachmann puts Crooked Fingers to rest and releases an album simply called Eric Bachmann.

years.h: Reason in Decline, the first Archers of Loaf album in 25 years
years.p: Eric Bachmann's energy goes to [[Archers of Loaf|7cf05db3-24e7-4534-84bf-65006cd0cc82]], whose Reason in Decline is their first full album since the 1990s.

eras.title: Heavy enough to need a band
eras.text: Merge's reissues of the old records nudged Eric Bachmann back to the name, and the new songs were too loud and too full of death to be a solo album.

years.big: It made me wish I had a band
q: It was heavy, and it made me wish that I had a band.
years.p: Eric Bachmann says the songs he was writing weren't mellow like a solo album, so he brought back the Crooked Fingers name.

years.h: Eric Bachmann's heart scare on Halloween
years.p: Eric Bachmann told Sun 13 he was found to have a 100 percent blockage of his right coronary artery on Halloween 2025. His body had grown natural bypasses, and doctors are watching it closely.

years.cap: Swet Deth, Merge, 2026. Artwork by Eric Bachmann's son
years.h: Swet Deth, the first Crooked Fingers album in 15 years
years.p: Merge releases Swet Deth with guests [[Sharon Van Etten|5a2e9cd3-010a-4aae-9f83-629253284202]], [[Matt Berninger|991813f5-27c6-4ff3-88dd-90e750dad545]] of [[The National|664c3e0e-42d8-48c1-b209-1efca19c0325]] and Merge boss [[Mac McCaughan|8841967d-3914-4ab9-aca6-94781aa35288]], who sings on the single Cold Waves.
years.xp:
Eric Bachmann's son made the cover. Bachmann said he didn't mean to write about death; it was just what was there. Liz Durrett sings on it too.

Bachmann, now living in Athens, Georgia, said he wouldn't tour until his heart condition was resolved.
